strengths: The paper addresses a well-motivated and underexplored problem in VLA-based autonomous driving: the lack of a principled exploration mechanism during RL post-training and the sparsity of supervision from text/trajectory labels alone.

The core idea of using world-model image-prediction uncertainty (entropy over discrete RGB/depth tokens) as an intrinsic, safety-gated exploration reward for GRPO is conceptually elegant and, to my knowledge, a novel way to distinguish genuine OOD discovery from mere expert imitation in the driving-VLA setting.

Strong empirical results: SOTA PDMS (93.7) and EPDMS (88.8) on NAVSIM v1/v2, notably outperforming several multi-camera/LiDAR methods while using only a single front-view camera, which is a meaningful efficiency/impact claim.

Reasonably thorough ablations isolate the contributions of (a) RGB vs depth generation as dense supervision and (b) PDMS reward vs image-based exploration reward in Stage 2, clarifying which components matter.

Qualitative results (Fig. 3, Fig. 4, Fig. 6) provide intuitive, concrete illustrations of how the exploration bonus differs from naive L2-distance novelty and how RL post-training corrects specific safety-critical planning failures.
Additional validation on nuScenes (Stage 1 only) and detailed implementation/hyperparameter disclosure in the appendix support reproducibility.
weaknesses: Fig. 3 (left) shows the exploration bonus is generally positively correlated with L2 error to the expert trajectory, which raises the question of how much genuinely new information the costlier world-model-uncertainty signal provides beyond a simple L2-based novelty term; only a single qualitative counterexample (Fig. 3, right) is given rather than a systematic quantitative comparison (e.g., an ablation replacing the image-uncertainty bonus with an L2-based bonus under the same safety gating).

The measured gain from the exploration bonus itself is modest: in Table 4, adding the image reward alone barely changes PDMS (88.50→88.53), and combining it with the PDMS reward only improves PDMS by 0.17 over PDMS-reward-alone (90.19→90.36). Without variance/significance information, it is hard to be confident this improvement is not noise, which somewhat undercuts the paper's central exploration-reward contribution.

The entropy-based uncertainty measure conflates epistemic uncertainty (true OOD novelty) with aleatoric uncertainty (scenes that are inherently visually complex/ambiguous, e.g., cluttered intersections, occlusions, lighting variation); the paper does not analyze or control for this confound, which could bias the exploration bonus toward visually complex but not necessarily novel-behavior scenarios.

Depth supervision is derived from a pretrained monocular depth estimator (Metric3D) rather than sensor ground truth, meaning the “geometric supervision” signal is itself a noisy pseudo-label; potential error propagation or bias inherited from this depth network is not discussed.

The safety threshold δ and exploration weight λ appear to be fixed by hand (0.9 and 0.5) without a sensitivity study, leaving unclear how robust the method is to these choices, which could materially affect the safety/exploration trade-off.

Comparisons in Table 1/2 mix single-camera, multi-camera, and multi-camera+LiDAR methods; while the paper appropriately notes ExploreVLA's single-camera setting, framing it as outperforming multi-sensor SOTA slightly overstates the comparison since sensing modality is a substantial confound for driving performance.

RL post-training is only demonstrated on NAVSIM; nuScenes results use Stage 1 only because of the lack of closed-loop reward signals there, so the generality of the full two-stage framework (its main contribution) is validated on a single benchmark family.

No discussion of the computational overhead of running the world model (image generation + entropy computation) for every rollout during GRPO training, which could be a substantial practical cost relative to trajectory-only RL baselines and is relevant to reproducibility/scalability claims.
